| |
---
Hi friend — People assume that frustration with government is a partisan thing. It’s not. It’s a you-don’t-know-a-guy thing or a you-don’t-write-a-big-enough-check thing. It can and does happen in any party. So before we get into it: if you’re ready for a government that answers to all of us and serves everyone equally, then I need you to help my team reach our really important end-of-month goal and use this personalized link to make a donation: **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sue_mayeom#chip-in](https://sue4ri.com/l/VVJy5SIqRFuf)** Now, the reason I know all of this is because I’ve had conversations across Rhode Island with people who don’t agree on much. Different towns, different backgrounds, different politics. Yet there’s one thing that comes up across all of them: the sense that the government isn’t really built for them. That there’s a version of it that works — if you have the connections, if you know the right people, if you’ve been navigating it long enough to know which levers to pull. And then there’s the version everyone else gets. That feeling is not a bug. It’s the result of a system that has slowly, consistently been made to serve the people with special access to it rather than the people it’s supposed to serve. Lobbyists. Insiders. Donors with the “right connections.” **_The antidote to entrenched, corrupt government isn’t a better lobbyist. It’s an office that actually opens its doors._** Here’s what I do on the Providence City Council: I explain things. I hold our government and the council I sit on accountable to the people it’s supposed to work for. I’ve built a track record that has nothing to do with who you know or what you can afford. I take responsibility and answer questions honestly — and _listen_ to everyone — regardless of whether we agree or disagree. That’s the version of the LG’s office I want to build. Government that reads like Schoolhouse Rock for adults, not like something you need a lawyer or a lobbyist to navigate. But running for office statewide requires resources to put that message everywhere — mailboxes, digital ads, organizing across all 39 municipalities — because the system that benefits from opacity is already well-funded.

| Peter,

Sometimes it's hard to believe anyone in Washington cares about the problems you and your neighbors are facing.

**I know that's what I've been hearing from Iowans on the campaign trail lately.** They wonder why Mariannette Miller-Meeks isn't doing anything to help them. Why does she keep voting against our district's interests and communities? This is unacceptable. No one should ever wonder if their representative is working to serve them or working to serve corporate donors and party bosses in DC.

## Lisa Ramirez Unites Voters Across Party Lines as Volunteer Army Rises to Challenge Incumbents
---
| | Lisa Ramirez, candidate for California’s 40th Congressional District, has bridged the political divide, garnering more cross-party support than any other candidate in the crowded field. With the June primary on Tuesday, the Ramirez campaign has built an "army" of hundreds of volunteers—a group that includes a steadfast Democratic base alongside a surprising number of Republican and independent voters. This cross-party coalition sets Ramirez apart from her opponents, including incumbent Representatives Ken Calvert and Young Kim. While political experts have labeled CA-40 as a safe Republican seat, current data suggests a shift in voter sentiment. President Trump’s approval rating in the district has dipped to 37.7%, with Republicans comprising only 40% of all registered voters, opening a clear path for a candidate who can reach beyond traditional party silos. Internal polling of 1,895 voters–including 500 registered Republican and independent voters—suggests a path to the Top 2 for Ramirez with 23% of voter support in the crowded race. "We are uniting across socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and political party lines," said Lisa Ramirez. "Our movement is proof that money isn't speech and corporations are not people. When we prioritize neighbor-to-neighbor conversations over expensive ad buys, we build a community that cannot be bought," she continued. Ramirez’s grassroots momentum is matched by overwhelming support from the Democratic base. She has secured a minimum of 70% of the vote from every Democratic Club whose members vote in the endorsement process. Despite being the last to enter the race, Ramirez earned 52% of the delegate vote–more support than the other two Democratic candidates combined–at the California Democratic Party Convention, representing over 160,000 registered voters in the District. The Ramirez campaign strategy focuses on "people-power," prioritizing door-to-door engagement and local relationships over the 7-figure budgets of the opposition. Ramirez, a certified immigration law specialist, has a long track record of service, recently earning national attention for defeating ICE in court to secure the release of a local father of 3 U.S. Marines. "Voters are looking for leaders who don't just talk the talk, but walk the walk," Ramirez stated. "This campaign is not about me; it is about 'We.' We are fighting for the heart of this country, rooted in love and service to our neighbors.” With absentee ballots reaching over 465,000 voters, the Ramirez campaign continues to expand its volunteer-led efforts through Election Day in cities across the district, spanning Anaheim Hills south to Mission Viejo, Ladera Ranch east to Menifee, and north again from Murrieta to Corona. subject: What rulings will SCOTUS hand down in June?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by United for Democracy
body:
June is here. That means Supreme Court decisions are coming. | |
---
Peter, June is the busiest month of the year for the Supreme Court—that’s when they hand down their biggest wave of decisions. **The rulings we’re expecting this June could spell disaster for millions.** The extremist Supreme Court justices are fresh off their decision to gut voting rights, disenfranchise Black and Brown voters across the country, and tip the scales in favor of Republicans in the midterms. Ruling after ruling from this Court has taken power from everyday, working people and given it straight to the wealthy. They’ve given Donald Trump the power of a king in America. And they’ve helped build a rigged economy in which families struggle to afford rent, gas, groceries, and healthcare. **The decisions they have left on the docket could make things even worse.** Just take birthright citizenship. The Supreme Court heard that case this spring, with Trump attending the deliberations in person to intimidate them. And while reporting shows that they appeared skeptical, it’s still possible that they could strip birthright citizenship from immigrant communities across the country. We’re expecting some major cases to come down in the month ahead—ones that could affect trans rights, guns, and campaign finance. Our experts, activists, and allied organizations are gearing up for a huge response to each:
* **_Wolford v. Lopez_** -__ The Court could strike down another commonsense law, this time in Hawaii, **making it harder for states to keep guns out of public spaces.**
* **_West Virginia v. B.P.J._****and**** _Little v. Hecox_** -__ The Court could **uphold bans on trans children from playing sports** with their peers—building on last year's ruling that already stripped healthcare access.
* **_NRSC v. FEC_****** -**** Another ruling could tear down the few remaining campaign spending limits still in place after _Citizens United_ , **letting wealthy donors pour even more money into our elections** through political parties.

The bought-and-paid- for justices think no one can hold them accountable. Now that they’ve struck at the heart of the _Voting Rights Act_ , they’re poised to make even more toxic decisions. Some are preparing to retire and cement their extremist legacy with one last big case. **We can’t allow the wealthy, powerful extremists who have captured our justice system, warped our economy, and stolen our power to do so without a fight. They can’t be met with silence—we have to meet them with a big, coordinated, people-powered mass response.** That’s exactly what United for Democracy is here to do. We’re organizing with allied groups, activists, experts, and organizers across the country to make sure our demands for a political system that works for working people can’t be ignored. Whatever the next ruling is, whenever it drops, we’ll be ready. **Together, we can unrig the system the Supreme Court has helped warp and bring power back to the people.** [**June is here, and we need to respond rapidly to every ruling the Supreme Court sets down. clean_body: June is here. That means Supreme Court decisions are coming. | | Peter, June is the busiest month of the year for the Supreme Court—that’s when they hand down their biggest wave of decisions. The rulings we’re expecting this June could spell disaster for millions. The extremist Supreme Court justices are fresh off their decision to gut voting rights, disenfranchise Black and Brown voters across the country, and tip the scales in favor of Republicans in the midterms. Ruling after ruling from this Court has taken power from everyday, working people and given it straight to the wealthy. They’ve given Donald Trump the power of a king in America. And they’ve helped build a rigged economy in which families struggle to afford rent, gas, groceries, and healthcare. The decisions they have left on the docket could make things even worse. Just take birthright citizenship. The Supreme Court heard that case this spring, with Trump attending the deliberations in person to intimidate them. And while reporting shows that they appeared skeptical, it’s still possible that they could strip birthright citizenship from immigrant communities across the country. We’re expecting some major cases to come down in the month ahead—ones that could affect trans rights, guns, and campaign finance. Our experts, activists, and allied organizations are gearing up for a huge response to each: Wolford v. Lopez - The Court could strike down another commonsense law, this time in Hawaii, making it harder for states to keep guns out of public spaces. West Virginia v. B.P.J.and Little v. Hecox - The Court could uphold bans on trans children from playing sports with their peers—building on last year's ruling that already stripped healthcare access. NRSC v. FEC**** - Another ruling could tear down the few remaining campaign spending limits still in place after Citizens United , letting wealthy donors pour even more money into our elections through political parties. The bought-and-paid- for justices think no one can hold them accountable. Now that they’ve struck at the heart of the Voting Rights Act , they’re poised to make even more toxic decisions. Some are preparing to retire and cement their extremist legacy with one last big case. We can’t allow the wealthy, powerful extremists who have captured our justice system, warped our economy, and stolen our power to do so without a fight. They can’t be met with silence—we have to meet them with a big, coordinated, people-powered mass response. That’s exactly what United for Democracy is here to do. We’re organizing with allied groups, activists, experts, and organizers across the country to make sure our demands for a political system that works for working people can’t be ignored. Whatever the next ruling is, whenever it drops, we’ll be ready. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. ---|---|---
WOOF!! Hi humans!!! 🐾
It's me, Bailey! The official campaign dog for Haley Stevens. 🐶
My mom, Katelyn, is Haley Stevens' finance director, which means every day she sits down at her screen machine (aka computer) and starts saying things like:
"End of the month is almost here," and "We have to close the gap," and "Jeez, I need coffee."
And I'm like MOM. YOU ARE LITERALLY AN ANGEL, BUT I CAN SMELL YOUR STRESS. LET'S GO CHASE SQUIRRELS! 🐾
But apparently, Senate campaigns do not run on dog kisses (rude), so I'm coming to you today, fresh off a three-hour nap on the floor of campaign headquarters, in my official capacity as emotional support dog for the entire Team Haley pack.
**Because we have a super important fundraising goal coming up, and there is some real anxious zoomie energy from my humans around this end-of-month deadline.**
Which is apparently tonight? I don't totally understand time. I am literally a dog. Every day is wonderful as long as my mom is here and I get 17 to 200 pets a day.
But let me get human-level serious for a second. You know that thing where humans lower their voices, make eye contact, and stop petting me? Pretend that's my vibe right now:
From what I can gather this deadline matters.
Because it's one of those moments when campaigns have to show they've got momentum.
And if momentum is measured in joyful hustling? THEN WE GOT IT, BESTIE. 🐾
I see how people out on the campaign trail love Haley, and she loves them right back. She's hugging people, talking to voters, fighting for working families, and saying things like "I will fight for you" - and she still has time to tell me I'm a good girl and give me treats.
Honestly, I would vote for her to be my senator. But dogs do not participate in democracy. Yet!
So, while I personally believe the answer to most problems is more naps, the humans are telling me what they really need before midnight is grassroots support.
(Which, just to be clear, is different from eating grass. Which I will admit I sometimes do for fun and for other reasons that I genuinely cannot explain.)
Grassroots support is people coming together to do something bigger than themselves. Something that helps their neighbors. Something full of hope, and love, and Michigan energy.
I love that. That's basically everything good! You can practically smell the community.
**So this is my official reminder: If you 've been meaning to give human dollars (aka money) before the deadline tonight, now would be an extremely paws-itive time to do it.**
**[Also, if you donate, my mom will probably say"YES!!" and then maybe give me a treat, so I do need to be honest that this is a slightly selfish ask.](https://substack.com/redirect/a73b1c11-9fdc-4b3f-863b-0c19d982fe13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/a73b1c11-9fdc-4b3f-863b-0c19d982fe13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
OK! I gotta go now because I have a zoomies appointment, and if I miss it, I'm going to be insufferable.
Thank you for reading this! I love you!
Tail wags,
Bailey 🐶
Official Team Haley campaign dog

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

Dear Peter,
With two days until the primary, I want to write directly to you and make clear what we’re up against.
My opponents have flooded this race with corporate checks and MAGA money trying to drown me out and buy their win instead.
I’m fighting for working Californians: eliminating state income tax for those making under $100,000, winning single-payer health care, and lowering everyday costs.
**Californians don’t want talking points, they want leadership rooted in serving people, not billionaires and corporations.**
Unlike my opponents, I’m not taking corporate PAC cash, Big Oil money, or writing personal checks to my own campaign.
Instead, I’ve counted on Porter Supporters like you, Peter, at every turn on the campaign trail.
In these next two days, we need to get our message in front of every undecided voter before the polls close, and secure our spot on November’s ballot.

---
Ken Burns here, friend. I’ve said this before and it’s now more relevant than ever: The power rests in our hands to secure the future of the Senate.
**_[I have more to say, but if you want to use that power in your own hands, and have a few bucks to spare, please consider donating to Roy Cooper’s campaign before his end-of-month deadline tonight at midnight. Winning his race is absolutely critical if we’re going to flip the Senate, so I hope you’ll join me.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/12512?t=8&akid=1584%2E124072%2EV3V6Y1)_**
Across this country, people are feeling the strain in ways that don’t always make the history books – but shape lives all the same. The cost of groceries that are too high. A lifesaving prescription that forces a difficult choice. A paycheck that doesn’t just stretch as far as it once did.
These are the quiet pressures that define a moment.

Roy Cooper has spent much of his life as a public servant working to ease those burdens.
Not seeking attention, but doing the work. Expanding access to affordable health care. Investing in public schools. Defending the idea that government, at its best, is not distant – but present, steady and accountable to the people it serves.
It is the kind of leadership that rarely makes noise. But over time, it leaves a mark.

There are those who would take the state in a different direction – who see division as a strategy, who mistake power for purpose. They are organized. They are well-funded by dark-money groups.
**_[We can beat them back. This work matters, and we won’t stop fighting. So please, will you chip in before midnight to help elect Roy Cooper for the U.S. Senate?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/12512?t=9&akid=1584%2E124072%2EV3V6Y1)_**
| | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/12513?amount=5&t=10&akid=1584%2E124072%2EV3V6Y1)
---
History has been written in moments like this – when people choose not to sit back, but to take part.
If you can, _[**give today**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/12512?t=11&akid=1584%2E124072%2EV3V6Y1)_. Help ensure that the next chapter of North Carolina reflects the very best of what this state has always tried to be.
Thank you for doing your part,

Ken Burns

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

subject: This is what solidarity looks like
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260531-2319-foote&t=1001&akid=2319%2E342411%2E5_PSSX ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter,

Tonight is the Squad Victory Fund’s [ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260531-movement.5RyXnK&refcode=em20260531-2319&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=2319%2E342411%2E5_PSSX ]end-of-month fundraising deadline,
and I want to be honest with you: this movement only works when people
keep showing up for one another.

Every day, we’re up against powerful interests that want people exhausted,
divided, and convinced that change is impossible.

They scapegoat immigrants, attack our rights, and protect a system where
billionaires and corporations are heard first while working families are
pushed aside.

But I still believe in the power of people coming together to build
something better. I believe in neighbors organizing for each other, in
communities refusing to give up on justice, and in movements that keep
pushing forward even when the odds are stacked against us.

That’s how Alexandria, Ayanna, Rashida, and I got to Congress in the first
place.

Not because corporate PACs funded us or party insiders cleared the way. We
got here because people believed they deserved leaders who would fight
unapologetically for working families.

The truth is, we have some tough fights ahead. Primary season is already
underway, and we’re less than six months away from November’s elections.

Every fundraising goal we hit helps us build the resources we need to
defend our seats, organize in our communities, and keep delivering real
change.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260531-movement.5RyXnK&refcode=em20260531-2319&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=2319%2E342411%2E5_PSSX ]So I’m asking,

deadline to keep Alexandria, Ayanna, Rashida, and me in the fight?

Derek, May was not business as usual. Not even close. In the span of a few weeks, Donald Trump made his intentions crystal clear — and they should alarm every single one of us. First, he announced “election integrity teams” to fan out across the country — **a thinly veiled effort to intimidate voters and dispute any result he doesn’t like.** Then he announced a **$1.776 billion bailout** — your tax dollars — for the rioters and election deniers who tried to overturn the will of the American people. **_I refuse to let that stand. And I have announced legislation to block it cold._** But Trump and his MAGA allies will throw everything they’ve got at stopping us. **[Will you chip in $5 before tonight’s end-of-month deadline to show them we won’t be intimidated?](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1230?c0=q22026_abs_em.Lvebai&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_EOM_AC90_20260531_AM1_V1_S1&email=&t=4&akid=9831%2E5257348%2Eyjgv35)** | [CHIP IN $5](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1230?c0=q22026_abs_em.Lvebai&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_EOM_AC90_20260531_AM1_V1_S1&email=&t=5&akid=9831%2E5257348%2Eyjgv35)

body:
Sustainer Sunday
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260531-2866)
Peter,
Quick PSA before our regularly scheduled Sustainer Sunday storytime.
Tonight at midnight, we hit our end-of-month fundraising deadline, and this is a big one. When the numbers go public, they're a signal of where this campaign is headed and whether we've got the resources to take the fight to the next level.
We've all been working so hard for this. Tonight's the night we ask you to go all in with us. Click the link below, chip in what you can, then come right back.
[**Give before midnight.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260531.9_yN1Y&refcode=em20260531-2866&t=1&akid=2866%2E105371%2EejWxRa)
Okay — now back to the good stuff. This week, we’re sharing a story from Eva Wingren, a working mom in Madison who happens to be one of Fran's own constituents.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260531.9_yN1Y&refcode=em20260531-2866&t=2&akid=2866%2E105371%2EejWxRa)
* * *
_"Fran is my state rep, but I didn't realize how cool she was until an organizing comrade recommended our group work on her campaign. He knows her personally and was willing to make a big commitment because he was excited — and he knew others would be, too._
**_That's what's going to win us elections: someone who gets people excited about politics and drives turnout._**
_Fran's care platform really speaks to me. As a working mom of a toddler, I need high-quality childcare — and that can only come from workers whose wages let them thrive. I've also had several big medical experiences recently, and I come from a medical family. The long waits for hospital admittance, the long waits just to be assigned a primary care doctor — they have me scared for the future of our health care system. We're all going to need it at some point._
**_There are folks in my network who think Democrats need to run a centrist to win statewide. To that I say: The polling and the recent election results are telling us that progressive populists can win, even in purple states._**
_I don't want to spend the next six months arguing with my own coalition about holding our noses for the lesser of two evils — I'd rather be bringing independents in on the basis of broadly appealing worker protections._
_Aren't you hungry for a candidate who's actually worth throwing down for?"_
**— Eva Wingren, Madison**
* * *
Fran isn't asking anyone to settle — she's showing us that a better world is possible.
Tonight's deadline is how we prove that we make better possible.
We're up against the clock, we're up against the big donors, and we're up against attacks from people who want to keep the status quo in place.
[Chip in $10, $15, or $25 a month before midnight and let's close this month strong.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260531.9_yN1Y&refcode=em20260531-2866&t=3&akid=2866%2E105371%2EejWxRa)
[**Become a monthly sustainer today.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260531.9_yN1Y&refcode=em20260531-2866&t=4&akid=2866%2E105371%2EejWxRa)
Thanks for being in this with us.
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260531.9_yN1Y&amount=5&refcode=em20260531-2866&t=7&akid=2866%2E105371%2EejWxRa)**
With gratitude,
Team Hong
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260531-2866&t=8&refcode2=2866_105371_ejWxRa&akid=2866%2E105371%2EejWxRa)**

I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.

_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.

That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.

That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here."

**P.S.** Peter, what you're seeing right now is something we've been working toward for years -- a generation of young Americans who are no longer willing to sit quietly while the Left dominates their schools and culture.

But moments like this don't sustain themselves.

If we don't keep up, we lose ground. It's that simple.

**We need to keep pace with the growth happening right now -- to fund more activism kits, support more chapters, and make sure no student is left standing alone after they decide to speak up. **

clean_body: I think this is where things are heading | | | | | Peter, I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground. Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible. Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them. They're already claimed. And we don't have extras. By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in. Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it. That's where things stand right now. We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment. And I don't say that lightly. Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down. The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great. And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing. Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back. We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there. And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet. That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens. And it's not isolated growth anymore. We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America. That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation... And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak. So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build. What's different now is the pace. Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: ✅ Arkansas ✅ Florida ✅ Idaho ✅ Indiana ✅ Montana ✅ Nebraska ✅ Oklahoma ✅ South Carolina ✅ Texas ✅ Tennessee That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action. That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly. It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up. Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through. And right now, that's where we're stretched. We're not lacking interest or momentum. We're working to keep up with both. So here 's how you can help... Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it. An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: ✅ Constitutions. ✅ Chapter guides. ✅ Flags. ✅ Materials to organize and lead. It turns a student who wants to speak up... into one who actually does. And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here." Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines. That's how we keep saying "yes" when the next student steps forward. That's how this movement actually scales. Because the reality is, the demand is here now. The only question is whether we're equipped to meet it. And that comes down to whether people like you decide to step in and help carry this forward. One final thing: I also wanted to say thank you. If you've supported Turning Point USA before -- whether once or many times -- you've already played a role in building what you're seeing right now. Students finding their voice. More state partnerships. New TPUSA chapters like the one at Charlie's former high school. This kind of momentum doesn't happen without people willing to stand behind it. And we don't take that lightly. I appreciate you taking the time to read this, and for everything you've already done to support this work. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. Peter, what you're seeing right now is something we've been working toward for years -- a generation of young Americans who are no longer willing to sit quietly while the Left dominates their schools and culture. But moments like this don't sustain themselves. If we don't keep up, we lose ground. It's that simple. We need to keep pace with the growth happening right now -- to fund more activism kits, support more chapters, and make sure no student is left standing alone after they decide to speak up. If you've already supported Turning Point USA in the past, thank you for carrying this movement forward every single day. If you haven't yet, I'm asking you to step in now. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

subject: I’ll always stand ten toes down for St. Louis

body:

If you know me, you know I’m always ten toes down for St. Louis.
That’s why, while I was in Congress, I fought every single day to deliver record federal funding back home to our communities, because St. Louis deserves investment, opportunity, and leaders who will never stop fighting for working people.
And it’s why I’ve never stayed silent about the historic disinvestment of North St. Louis or the Republican-led attacks on our city’s right to govern itself.
For far too long, Black and brown communities in St. Louis have been treated like political targets instead of communities worthy of care, safety, and resources. The same politicians starving our neighborhoods of investment are the ones trying to strip power away from local residents and impose state control over our police and our future.
I don’t believe billionaires, extremists in Jefferson City, or out-of-touch politicians know what’s best for St. Louis.
The people do.
We deserve leaders who will fight to protect our right to self-governance, invest in our communities rather than criminalize them, and finally address the decades of neglect North St. Louis has endured.
That fight is bigger than one election. It’s about building power for everyday people—and refusing to let corporate interests and extremist politicians decide who deserves resources, safety, and dignity.
My primary is in exactly 65 days. If you’re with me in this fight for St. Louis, will you chip in before our end-of-month deadline to help us keep organizing and building people-powered momentum? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q2?refcode=x_260531_tentoes_eom3_act]
DONATE BEFORE MIDNIGHT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q2?refcode=x_260531_tentoes_eom3_act]
I’ll never stop fighting for our city.
In solidarity,
Cori Bush

most extreme legal theories.

decided, brushed off criticism of Supreme Court corruption as a “smear
campaign,” and complained that prosecutors should have dropped Trump’s
criminal cases because they interfered with his return to power.

Subtle? Not even close.

Trump isn’t nominating Flowers because he’s fair or qualified. He’s
nominating him because he’s already proven he’ll be a reliable rubber
stamp for the MAGA agenda from the bench.

This is the game: pack the courts with young extremists, hand them

Patriot,
In 2023, our team conducted our first domestic rescue in California.
**A 12-year-old girl.** _Trafficked. Drugged. Raped. Held for 45 days in a homeless encampment under a bridge._
_**Our operators physically extracted her.** _
What it takes to be that team is what most people never see. The training. The intelligence work. The willingness to walk into a homeless encampment under a bridge knowing exactly what you might find and what you might have to do to bring a child out alive. The capacity to stay steady when the place you are going to is the worst place a 12-year-old has ever been.
**And underneath all of it, faith.** Our operators are vetted under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure before they ever set foot on a mission – because the work breaks anyone who walks into it without something stronger than their own will to fall back on. **We are the hands and feet of Jesus Christ in the field, and we have been since the day this organization started.** That is not a slogan. It is the load-bearing piece of how a team walks under that bridge and walks back out with a 12-year-old girl alive.
Thanks to God and the work of our operators, she made it home. Her family will never be the same. Neither will our team.
She was one of nine children we recovered in California that year. Each one is a blessing, but know this – _the next child is already missing._
**This is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Force Recon scout sniper with two decades of service and 15 overseas deployments. Today, I write to you as the Founder and CEO of Heroes for Humanity.**

**We were forged in the fire of the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, when I went behind enemy lines to bring 77 Americans and Afghan allies home. Fast forward, and today we are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit network of veteran special operators, first responders, and medical professionals doing the work most organizations cannot.**
In the last 90 days alone, our team has operated across three continents – efforts which entailed:
**✅ Eight American families extracted **from Mexico in February.

**✅ 33 American families and 155 additional Americans** assisted across Israel, Egypt, and Jordan in March.

**✅ 100,000+ meals distributed to individuals in desperate need in Haiti**.

**✅ Three more young teenage children rescued from trafficking situations** in Virginia and West Texas this January.
The work goes back further. **64 evacuated from Ukraine** during active combat in 2022. **58 Christians rescued from persecution** across Asia-Pacific and granted asylum.
For five years we have done all of this from temporary facilities, borrowed space, and on-the-fly logistics. We made it work because we had to. But the demand keeps accelerating, and we cannot train operators fast enough this way.
**So we've just launched an intensive, nationwide capital campaign for the Heroes for Humanity National Training Center – a permanent home for the mission, right here in our home state of Texas.**
**The Training Center is a permanent facility built around the three pillars of our mission – precision personnel rescues, humanitarian and medical aid, and evangelism.** Standardized certification for every operator we put in the field. Medical and trauma training for austere and hostile environments. An OSINT and intelligence hub for ongoing mission planning. And the capacity to train the next generation of operators – at scale, under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure – for as long as the mission lasts.
**Total goal:** $1,000,000 by October.
**First milestone:** $100,000.

**As we approach Memorial Day, I would be remiss to not highlight a central piece of the facility, our Foundational Wall** – our way of honoring those who've served, and other heroes among us who deserve our gratitude. **For gifts of $1,000 or more, you can dedicate a brick in honor of someone you choose.** For service members, information will include name, unit, branch, birth and end dates. For non-service members, information may include personal details and attributes, “in loving memory of,” and birth and end dates.
**While that 12-year-old girl in California is now safe, countless other missing children are already out there.** Please, help us build the place that prepares our operators to go find, and bring them home.

clean_body: For five years, we have done this work from temporary facilities and borrowed space, with on-the-fly logistics. | | | | | | Patriot, In 2023, our team conducted our first domestic rescue in California. A 12-year-old girl. Trafficked. Drugged. Raped. Held for 45 days in a homeless encampment under a bridge. Our operators physically extracted her. What it takes to be that team is what most people never see. The training. The intelligence work. The willingness to walk into a homeless encampment under a bridge knowing exactly what you might find and what you might have to do to bring a child out alive. The capacity to stay steady when the place you are going to is the worst place a 12-year-old has ever been. And underneath all of it, faith. Our operators are vetted under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure before they ever set foot on a mission – because the work breaks anyone who walks into it without something stronger than their own will to fall back on. We are the hands and feet of Jesus Christ in the field, and we have been since the day this organization started. That is not a slogan. It is the load-bearing piece of how a team walks under that bridge and walks back out with a 12-year-old girl alive. Thanks to God and the work of our operators, she made it home. Her family will never be the same. Neither will our team. She was one of nine children we recovered in California that year. Each one is a blessing, but know this – the next child is already missing. This is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Force Recon scout sniper with two decades of service and 15 overseas deployments. Today, I write to you as the Founder and CEO of Heroes for Humanity. We were forged in the fire of the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, when I went behind enemy lines to bring 77 Americans and Afghan allies home. Fast forward, and today we are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit network of veteran special operators, first responders, and medical professionals doing the work most organizations cannot. In the last 90 days alone, our team has operated across three continents – efforts which entailed: ✅ Eight American families extracted from Mexico in February. ✅ 33 American families and 155 additional Americans assisted across Israel, Egypt, and Jordan in March. ✅ 100,000+ meals distributed to individuals in desperate need in Haiti. ✅ Three more young teenage children rescued from trafficking situations in Virginia and West Texas this January. The work goes back further. 64 evacuated from Ukraine during active combat in 2022. 58 Christians rescued from persecution across Asia-Pacific and granted asylum. For five years we have done all of this from temporary facilities, borrowed space, and on-the-fly logistics. We made it work because we had to. But the demand keeps accelerating, and we cannot train operators fast enough this way. So we've just launched an intensive, nationwide capital campaign for the Heroes for Humanity National Training Center – a permanent home for the mission, right here in our home state of Texas. The Training Center is a permanent facility built around the three pillars of our mission – precision personnel rescues, humanitarian and medical aid, and evangelism. Standardized certification for every operator we put in the field. Medical and trauma training for austere and hostile environments. An OSINT and intelligence hub for ongoing mission planning. And the capacity to train the next generation of operators – at scale, under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure – for as long as the mission lasts. Total goal: $1,000,000 by October. First milestone: $100,000. | "MAKE A GIFT TODAY" As we approach Memorial Day, I would be remiss to not highlight a central piece of the facility, our Foundational Wall – our way of honoring those who've served, and other heroes among us who deserve our gratitude. For gifts of $1,000 or more, you can dedicate a brick in honor of someone you choose. For service members, information will include name, unit, branch, birth and end dates. For non-service members, information may include personal details and attributes, “in loving memory of,” and birth and end dates. While that 12-year-old girl in California is now safe, countless other missing children are already out there. Please, help us build the place that prepares our operators to go find, and bring them home. Thank you, and let's never forget our mission – to free the oppressed, so others may live. Respectfully submitted, Dennis Price Founder & CEO Heroes for Humanity | | | | "PLEASE DONATE" | | | | | SERVING THE VULNERABLE. SHARING THE GOSPEL. name: Roy Cooper
subject: This is a long email
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
10,000 votes 10 years ago
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260531_2.Evy2-i&refcode=em20260531-2&t=1&akid=6936%2E582294%2EuynrHY)
At the end of this message, I’m going to ask you to split a $5 donation to my Senate campaign here in North Carolina and Chris Pappas. **[If you’re ready to give now, you can use this link to donate.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260531_2.Evy2-i&refcode=em20260531-2&t=2&akid=6936%2E582294%2EuynrHY)**
**Otherwise, please let me explain why your support is so important and what could happen without it.**
In 2016, I ran for Governor for the first time.
I was fighting to unseat Republican Governor Pat McCrory. Nobody had defeated an incumbent Governor in North Carolina for over 150 years, but I knew that we had the team behind us to win and make history.
Throughout the race, multiple election experts were saying it was a “Toss Up.” Poll after poll showed me with a slight – or sometimes even large – lead. The momentum was on our side.
**However, on Election Night, the race was too close to call.**
I ended that night with a less than 5,000-vote lead – which might sound like a lot but is a razor-thin margin in North Carolina, especially given the 4.6 million ballots cast. It was less than half of 1%.
Governor McCrory didn’t concede. He claimed that there had been voter fraud in our state with no evidence to back it up.
He called for a recount, and over the next month, he and his team continued spreading baseless conspiracy theories and undermining faith in the democratic process.
**Yet on Dec. 5, 2016, democracy won. The recount was wrapped up, and the results were in: We had won the race by 10,277 votes.**
This current Senate race is starting to remind me a lot of my 2016 race.
Just like in 2016, the momentum today appears to be on our side.
Experts are calling this race a “Toss Up.” Even though President Trump carried North Carolina each of the three times he ran, recent polling shows me statistically tied with his handpicked candidate. Even the experts are saying that this is the best chance for Democrats to flip a Republican-held seat in the country.
Here’s what worries me...
**We could have just as easily lost that race in 2016. Despite all of the winds blowing in our favor, we still only won by 10,277 votes – just 0.22%.**
That’s why we simply cannot take our foot off the gas. We cannot look at the polls and the predictions and think for a second that we have this in the bag. We cannot give our Republican opponent or the right-wing super PACs supporting him an inch.
**I won in 2016 – in the same election that President Trump first won the presidency – only because of grassroots support from people like you. That’s how I plan to win again, but I need you with me.**
**[Please: Will you split a $5 donation, or whatever you can, between our campaign and Chris Pappas to help us flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260531_2.Evy2-i&refcode=em20260531-2&t=3&akid=6936%2E582294%2EuynrHY)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260531_2.Evy2-i&amount=5&refcode=em20260531-2&t=22&akid=6936%2E582294%2EuynrHY)**
Thank you for reading. I appreciate it.
Roy Cooper

Friend, California does not bow down to tyrants.
My parents had me while working as social justice missionaries in the Philippines, and moved our family to California when I was just two months old to raise their children in a free society — where democracy was real, the rule of law meant something, and where every person could live with dignity and respect.
That’s the California they believed in — and that’s the California I’m fighting to protect.
As your Attorney General, I’ve fought to protect our freedoms wherever Trump has tried to undermine them. Bodily autonomy, the freedom to love who you love, access to health care, protection from corporate interests, and the right to live freely and without fear.
Every time this administration breaks the law, tramples our rights, and attacks our democracy, we fight back — again and again. And again and again, we win.
I’m doing everything I can to keep fighting for the same promise that brought my family here, and for the future generations who deserve to inherit that version of California, and that includes running for re-election this year.
Will you support my campaign today with a contribution of any amount before our May end-of-month deadline? The link to give is right here:

Peter,
This primary election, Oregon voters showed up for climate leadership, and together, we made it happen.
Thanks to supporters like you, OLCV and OLCV PAC helped elect and advance climate champions across Oregon, including some major victories in key legislative and local races.
In one of our top priority races, Senate District 15, voters chose OLCV-endorsed challenger Myrna Muñoz over a well-funded, corporate-backed incumbent. Myrna was inspired to run over proposed data center construction in her community and will be a climate and environmental champion in the legislature.
Across our priority races, we’re seeing positive results in nearly 73% of the races we invested in .These wins prove something important: when we organize, mobilize voters, and invest in bold climate leadership, we win.
This cycle, OLCV staff and volunteers knocked on more than 6,300 doors and contacted over 10,000 voters directly to help build support for candidates who will fight for climate action, accountability, and Oregon communities.
But, our work is far from over. The general election is just around the corner, and corporate interests are already preparing to spend heavily to stop climate progress in Oregon.

Fellow American, it's Newt Gingrich.

I am going to be straight with you, because that is the only way I know how to operate.

I have been sounding the alarm for months, telling anyone who will listen that our party needs to sharpen its message, connect with the American people on the issues that are hitting them hardest, and walk into November with a strategy that actually reflects the reality on the ground.

We must not sleepwalk into an election we should be winning and come up short because we were not paying close enough attention.

subject: I understand this better than most
body:
Hi there, it's Derek – I appreciate you opening my message.

I know you've heard a lot from me and other candidates running for Congress. Many of them may use scam tactics and "sky is falling" language to convince you to donate.

I am proud that we run a different campaign. From the beginning, I've made a point to center our communities in everything I do.

**And believe me: I flipped CA-45 by 653 votes. I understand the importance of every vote counting better than most.**

Now, I'm facing a whopping FIVE Republican challengers in my first re-election race – all who will carry out the MAGA status quo and do nothing about the real issues facing Orange and Los Angeles Counties.

Tuesday's primary is the first test of our strength after Proposition 50 added tens of thousands of new voters to the district. We're organizing until the end to reach as many as we can – and that takes serious resources.

**In short: I'm the most vulnerable Democratic incumbent in California, and one of the most at-risk in the entire country.**

If, and only if, you're able to donate, $3 will be a huge help in finishing strong on Tuesday. Will you chip in?

Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

body:
Grassroots donations are slowing. Republican fundraising is not. But this isn't over. |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132449751/624548013/-1282862128?sourceid=1058950&refcode=WUEFEQ99_20260531_EOMRecordRS_ALL_v1s4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZGMxYzk5Ny0xYTVkLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExODkwNWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VuthFLUji5Oj8O4dTRKxZxM7dXOVFbsVugIagF1P8wQ=) Hi Peter,

I want to be honest with you about where we stand.

Our grassroots donations have slowed down at exactly the wrong time. At a moment when Republicans are raising aggressively to hold onto power, fewer small-dollar donors are coming through the door for Democratic pro-choice women.

I understand why. Donor fatigue is real. Life is expensive — now more than ever. People are overwhelmed.

| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001cU9rlLI2BxRDh5ghHOURhMqIutF3Hmxr5oEkVA2nhC2MFsQMQqOWHnP0EHqJGwLr3Tp1XAIBjLIP7MucaGsAciA0ZP2TMVN1h0ytszmOk5ivZGC5lMw4CMllNEk_1fkuZ2bCvYqJI5V-D1RCYqZotGgY-Ee8uxYfMFaG641dNvsgLpt4VVpDPBFdaze0oXZAov2Ei3L21ucF0ltpkRK8__eCZvOFP_k-&c=-WrXwhADza7MLXDrCzAbcaCEIwnP4toxQi2zILsL7LLOmMzwMBUlMA==&ch=KeMiqOAucJMuNif19gIC1xp88GwTQ0skoNWSWuVMBt8LoIfsKEVOrw==)

|
Peter,
Something broke this week that connects every alarm we have raised about this Supreme Court into a single, damning picture.
Justice Samuel Alito's son has been secretly working as an attorney inside the Treasury Department since the early months of Trump's second term, briefed on the most sensitive legal matters across the entire department, offering counsel at the highest level on Treasury policy and law.
Alito's son was working inside the Treasury Department while a lawsuit challenging Trump's emergency powers landed before the court with the Treasury named as a defendant. He maintained no public profile, avoided giving his last name, and the Treasury never disclosed his employment in court filings. His father did not recuse himself.
The Treasury Department is now administering Trump's $1.8 billion "Anti-Weaponization Fund," taxpayer money with no congressional approval and no independent oversight, currently paying out to the January 6th insurrectionists Trump pardoned. Alito's son sits in the office providing legal oversight for that fund. When challenges reach the Supreme Court, they land in front of a bench that includes his father.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001cU9rlLI2BxRDh5ghHOURhMqIutF3Hmxr5oEkVA2nhC2MFsQMQqOWHnP0EHqJGwLr3Tp1XAIBjLIP7MucaGsAciA0ZP2TMVN1h0ytszmOk5ivZGC5lMw4CMllNEk_1fkuZ2bCvYqJI5V-D1RCYqZotGgY-Ee8uxYfMFaG641dNvsgLpt4VVpDPBFdaze0oXZAov2Ei3L21ucF0ltpkRK8_5AywtoqW_wl&c=-WrXwhADza7MLXDrCzAbcaCEIwnP4toxQi2zILsL7LLOmMzwMBUlMA==&ch=KeMiqOAucJMuNif19gIC1xp88GwTQ0skoNWSWuVMBt8LoIfsKEVOrw==)
---
This court is not just extreme. It is corrupt.
Clarence Thomas accepted years of luxury travel, private jet flights, and undisclosed vacation accommodations from a Texas billionaire with interests before the court. He never disclosed it or recused himself. When Congress demanded answers, the court stonewalled.
Samuel Alito accepted a private jet flight to an Alaskan fishing lodge from a conservative mega-donor. He flew a flag associated with the January 6th election denial movement outside his home. He declined to recuse himself from cases where conflicts were obvious. No accountability or consequences.
This is the court Leonard Leo built with $1.6 billion in dark money. The court that granted Trump criminal immunity. The court that gutted the Voting Rights Act. The court that opened the floodgates for the unlimited dark money that paid for all of it.
The only answer to a system this corrupt is to reform the institution at the top of it. That is what Unpack Our Courts is building, the movement to expand the court, establish term limits, and create the binding ethics code that would have made every abuse described above impossible.
That is the long game. The short game is to continue building a firewall of state Supreme Courts. We already built it in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, and this November we are taking it to Nevada, Kentucky, Montana, Michigan, and Minnesota, holding the line at the state level while we push federal reform through.

name: Voto Latino
subject: Participation
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
Protecting democracy doesn’t take deep pockets.
#
_Protecting democracy doesn’t take deep pockets, Peter._ It takes participation.
That is why Voto Latino is working every day from now til November to mobilize and register Latino voters and make sure they have the tools they need to participate in our democracy.
Right now, millions of eligible Latino voters are still unregistered, which is a gap that we’re working to narrow.
[**If you can, will you rush $3 or more right now to help register Latino voters?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260531-1-ak.Lqz9PO&amount=3&refcode=em20260531-194&t=1&akid=194%2E1366028%2E0rFzYg)
We’re one of the largest national organizations doing voter registration year-round in the country.
We’ve helped more than **9.5 million people navigate the voting process** by making it easier to register, check their status, find their polling place, and make a plan to vote.
We’ve also **registered 2 million voters**. In 2020 alone, we registered more than 650,000 voters, and 82% of those voters turned out to vote.
The work we do continues today because millions of eligible Latino voters are still unregistered, even as key elections are decided by razor-thin margins.
Voto Latino is focused on closing that gap by finding unregistered voters, helping them register, and making sure they have the information and support they need to cast a ballot. **But with the midterm election just 6 months away, there’s still a lot of work to do.**
We need to register more voters, reach more people, and continue building the strength of Latino participation.
We set a goal to raise **$10,000 by tonight** to fuel this critical work. We’re really close to reaching it, but we won’t without your help.
**[Will you give $3 today to help us reach our fundraising goal and power our voter registration efforts?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260531-1-ak.Lqz9PO&amount=3&refcode=em20260531-194&t=2&akid=194%2E1366028%2E0rFzYg)**

Thank you,
Voto Latino

I wanted to make sure you saw Sue’s latest email about the long list of things she’s heard from voters over the years. And how it drives this campaign. **Begin forwarded message:**
> ****
> Hi friend —
>
> People assume that frustration with government is a partisan thing.
>
> It’s not. It’s a you-don’t-know-a-guy thing or a you-don’t-write-a-big-enough-check thing. It can and does happen in any party.
>
> So before we get into it: if you’re ready for a government that answers to all of us and serves everyone equally, then I need you to help my team reach our really important end-of-month goal and use this personalized link to make a donation: **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sue_mayeom#chip-in](https://sue4ri.com/l/IQvBqQq9OZ41)**
>
> Now, the reason I know all of this is because I’ve had conversations across Rhode Island with people who don’t agree on much. Different towns, different backgrounds, different politics.
>
> Yet there’s one thing that comes up across all of them: the sense that the government isn’t really built for them. That there’s a version of it that works — if you have the connections, if you know the right people, if you’ve been navigating it long enough to know which levers to pull.
>
> And then there’s the version everyone else gets.
>
> That feeling is not a bug. It’s the result of a system that has slowly, consistently been made to serve the people with special access to it rather than the people it’s supposed to serve. Lobbyists. Insiders. Donors with the “right connections.”
>
> **_The antidote to entrenched, corrupt government isn’t a better lobbyist. It’s an office that actually opens its doors._**
>
> Here’s what I do on the Providence City Council: I explain things. I hold our government and the council I sit on accountable to the people it’s supposed to work for. I’ve built a track record that has nothing to do with who you know or what you can afford. I take responsibility and answer questions honestly — and listen to everyone — regardless of whether we agree or disagree.
>
> That’s the version of the LG’s office I want to build. Government that reads like Schoolhouse Rock for adults, not like something you need a lawyer or a lobbyist to navigate.
>
> But running for office statewide requires resources to put that message everywhere — mailboxes, digital ads, organizing across all 39 municipalities — because the system that benefits from opacity is already well-funded.
>
> | | **[We’re trying to bring in 250 new grassroots donors this month as proof that a different kind of politics is possible. Will you be one of them?
>
> CHIP IN TO HELP REACH 250 DONORS BY MAY 31 → ](https://sue4ri.com/l/5bzDRXxeDvai)** | | [ **DONATE** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/xY2UNE40KVLP)

>
> Together,
>
> Sue

name: Public Land Warriors
subject: Why Trump is moving the Forest Service
body:
This is a purge, plain and simple

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/K6Dw--giena0dM5mTeJrTA~~/AAUS1hA~/SDH6hWxEecZt_Znha282xd4zHZKoTQfRBiyKlfX-g1D5dCmjClwUmnsikKGpmJN-ZpwydbEnn4GbuKN_vTwt9FmaBOh1xQ7eF5MkRvfWmHr_JXsl_fniJe6r8f6mVGMA)
| | | | Peter, Let’s talk about why this government decided to uproot the U.S. Forest Service headquarters from Washington, D.C., and relocate it to Utah. The politicians pushing this are blanketing the airwaves with a convenient talking point: this is just about "bringing leadership closer to where the work happens." But that’s false. We know exactly what the strategy is here because we watched them run the exact same playbook in 2020. When the Bureau of Land Management headquarters was scattered out West, **almost 90% of the employees ordered to relocate chose to resign rather than uproot their families.** It stripped the agency of decades of institutional knowledge and effectively crippled it—which was precisely the point. The newest attack on the Forest Service goes even further. By moving headquarters, they are shuttering dozens of critical research centers and closing regional offices right before what is predicted to be a horrific wildfire season. Severing the Forest Service from the seat of power in Washington is a deliberate move to blindfold and bankrupt the agency. Over the last year, roughly a quarter of the Forest Service's 30,000 employees were already coerced or forced out. Now, thousands more are being handed relocation orders. If the BLM history is any guide, the Forest Service will soon be left with roughly half of its former ranks. As a result of this purge, campgrounds will close, trails will crumble, high fuel loads near communities will go unaddressed—making wildfires infinitely harder to fight. And when things inevitably start going wrong on the ground, the politicians who manufactured this crisis will throw up their hands, declare the federal government incompetent, and demand these public lands be sold off to private industry. **And just in case there was any doubt about their end game, look at where they are moving the agency: Utah.** They chose the home turf of Senator Mike Lee—the loudest architect of the public land selloff—and a state that is actively suing the federal government to take over millions of acres of your public lands. It is a bleak picture, but here is the good news: the inevitable does not need to happen. Because they are being so blatant about this corporate land grab, they are handing us the ammunition we need to stop them. The only thing that can prevent our forests from being mismanaged to the point of a fire sale is the organized, overwhelming outrage of the American people. clean_body: This is a purge, plain and simple | | | | | Peter, Let’s talk about why this government decided to uproot the U.S. Forest Service headquarters from Washington, D.C., and relocate it to Utah. The politicians pushing this are blanketing the airwaves with a convenient talking point: this is just about "bringing leadership closer to where the work happens." But that’s false. We know exactly what the strategy is here because we watched them run the exact same playbook in 2020. When the Bureau of Land Management headquarters was scattered out West, almost 90% of the employees ordered to relocate chose to resign rather than uproot their families. It stripped the agency of decades of institutional knowledge and effectively crippled it—which was precisely the point. The newest attack on the Forest Service goes even further. By moving headquarters, they are shuttering dozens of critical research centers and closing regional offices right before what is predicted to be a horrific wildfire season. Severing the Forest Service from the seat of power in Washington is a deliberate move to blindfold and bankrupt the agency. Over the last year, roughly a quarter of the Forest Service's 30,000 employees were already coerced or forced out. Now, thousands more are being handed relocation orders. If the BLM history is any guide, the Forest Service will soon be left with roughly half of its former ranks. As a result of this purge, campgrounds will close, trails will crumble, high fuel loads near communities will go unaddressed—making wildfires infinitely harder to fight. And when things inevitably start going wrong on the ground, the politicians who manufactured this crisis will throw up their hands, declare the federal government incompetent, and demand these public lands be sold off to private industry. And just in case there was any doubt about their end game, look at where they are moving the agency: Utah. They chose the home turf of Senator Mike Lee—the loudest architect of the public land selloff—and a state that is actively suing the federal government to take over millions of acres of your public lands. It is a bleak picture, but here is the good news: the inevitable does not need to happen. Because they are being so blatant about this corporate land grab, they are handing us the ammunition we need to stop them. The only thing that can prevent our forests from being mismanaged to the point of a fire sale is the organized, overwhelming outrage of the American people. They want to gut the agency in the shadows so they can sell off the land in broad daylight. Let’s make sure they fail. For the wild, Public Land Warriors | Public Land Warriors728 Gilbert StHelena, MT 59601United States "Website"

clean_body: State-by-state impact on the fight for fair maps and fair elections: | | | We shared big news on Friday: a generous donor has agreed to 2X-match grassroots donations through tonight's deadline. = This pro-democracy movement is rising up to meet a pivotal moment. Across the South, lawmakers are rushing to draw new voting maps that silence Black and brown voters. But across the South, with solidarity from all over the country, we are fighting back. We’re reaching out to voters in key states so they can call on their lawmakers to reject new gerrymanders. With this team’s support, we’ve made 20,000+ contacts in Alabama, 99,000+ contacts in Louisiana, 132,000+ contacts in Mississippi, 58,000+ contacts in Tennessee, and 312,000+ contacts here in Georgia, where a special map-rigging session starts in just a few weeks. = Recently, our co-founder, Stacey Abrams, testified before the Tennessee Senate Judiciary Committee and laid bare the stakes of this moment: “I come before you today though as a daughter of the South... because we are yoked together by geography and destiny. I did not travel to Tennessee today to weigh in on a policy debate or a political fight. “The question before you is whether America will continue the long, unfinished work of building a multi-racial, multi-ethnic, multi-generational democracy that belongs to all of us — or whether we will tear down the very protections that made that democracy finally possible.” —Stacey Abrams Our team also traveled to Montgomery, Alabama to rally for the National Day of Action on Voting Rights.
